Construct noun takes ascent alone. The phrase's single the is the article's under rule 29, so no determiner is supplied here; rule 29 supplies one on a construct only where no article morpheme is present or where the ASV writes a second the.

Corrected from unrepresented. The article stands on the nomen rectum and the ASV renders Ziz anarthrously, so this morpheme takes the one the written for the chain even though English fronts it to the left edge (rule 29, לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים → the two tables of stone). Rule 29's proper-name rider is explicit that an article MACULA segments off a toponym is never set aside as lexicalized in the name (בְּנֵי הָרָמָה → The children of Ramah), and the article is not spelled into this transliteration. Marking it unrepresented is reserved for a phrase the ASV writes no the for at all.

review_notes: Corrected the מַעֲלֵה הַצִּיץ chain: the ASV writes one the for the phrase and the rectum's article takes it under rule 29, English fronting it to the left edge, so the construct noun keeps only ascent. The accepted alignment had inverted this, supplying a the on the construct while a present article morpheme held nothing, against rules 2 and 29.

The two chains in this verse divide differently and the count is what tells them apart: the ascent of Ziz writes one the (fronted from the article), while the end of the valley writes two (each morpheme taking the one before its own word).
פְּנֵי here stands with no preposition and the ASV spends its one word on the relational lexeme, so the construct noun holds before (rule 19).
